about.text: Velveeta is a brand name for a processed cheese similar to American cheese. It was developed in 1918 by Emil Frey (1867–1951) of the Monroe Cheese Company in Monroe, New York. In 1923, The Velveeta Cheese Company was incorporated as a separate company. In 1925, it advertised two varieties, Swiss and American. The firm was purchased by Kraft Foods Inc. in 1927.

how.label: emulsify
how.text: Velveeta is built from milk, whey and milk protein concentrate with emulsifying phosphates and citrates rather than mainly from ripened cheese, which gives its soft, velvety melt. Because milk protein concentrate is not a permitted ingredient under the US process-cheese standards, it is labelled a 'pasteurized prepared cheese product'.
